svg.text: D15 — feedback composition, labelled sketch (2026-09-27, wave D15)

Hand-drawn SVG, no generated art (owner 2026-09-27). Implements ruling 18 (speed fantasy / feedback is cosmetic), ruling 23 (quadrants + breach malfunctions), UI_SPEC §3.10 A5.1 (flat chrome inside a pane), A5.2 (containers + anchors, chrome as stylebox/sibling, marks inside their own child rect), A5.4 (danger never colour alone).
1 · The quadrant feed lands on the status screen (right well)
RIGHT WELL (UI_SPEC §3.8 D7 mockup, well (316,60)–(696,348))
W1 · laser
W2 · mining
H1 · plate light
— appended pool rows, P8 order —
STERN 250 / 250
PORT 0 / 250
breach state (pool 0): 1 px accent_danger
frame on the row + the 0 figure itself —
never colour alone (A5.4)
Four `Label`s appended after the fit rows in the well's own container —
containers + anchors, no coordinates (A5.2(i)); flat caption text, no chrome
drawn over it (A5.1 / A5.2(ii)). Format stays "%s %d / %d" (PROW 250 / 250).
Feed: every status update the HUD pushes set_quadrants(prow, stern, port,
starboard) beside set_pools (hud.gd:_push_status; L241 closes). Breach read =
18 §4.5's malfunction state surfaced, zero gameplay numbers (ruling 18).
2 · The hit marker's visual verb: a strike (X) at the reticle centre
Verb: a strike — the X stamps where your fire landed.
accent_danger_bright, 4 px arms, 1 px width (shipped,
hud.gd:1960 HitMarker), 8×8 footprint over the reticle.
A5.2(iii): the mark draws inside its own full-rect child
of the reticle, never over HUD content.
Flash: alpha 1.0 → 0.0 over 0.25 s Tween (house rule: no
per-frame UI animation); a second hit restarts the tween,
so spam reads as one solid strike (anti-spam for free).
Fires per landed hit on any hull (S22 A1 / L28 — the pool-
drop poll becomes the hit_landed signal).
Verb language: strike = hit landed · steel ring (§1.5) = shield absorbed · chip burst = physical contact. Three events, three verbs.
3 · The ram spark lands at the contact point
One chip burst (fx_mining_beam f1..f4, 20 FPS,
0.2 s one-shot — FX-1's 3-object master) at the
contact point the handler already resolves
(player_ship.gd:472-492 / npc_ship.gd:538-548).
No §1.6 jitter disc — that scatter's readers stay
exactly three; a ram is one contact event.
Cue beside it: sfx_impact_hull (hull) /
sfx_impact_rock (rock) — S22 A2 / L56.
World-space FX under §7.3's wiring law (one-shot sheet, loop = false, animation_finished → queue_free); the A5 chrome law binds the Control surfaces in panels 1–2.
Owner rulings implemented

ruling 18 — speed fantasy / feedback is cosmetic: every element in this sketch is feedback; zero gameplay numbers live here (18 §3.4). The only feel rows that move gameplay (T-feel-1/1b seeker fuze) are flagged in the tick sheet, not drawn here.
ruling 23 — quadrants and breach malfunctions (18 §4.5): panel 1 surfaces the four pools and their breach state on the status screen; the S19 T1–T7 rows carry the mechanic.
A5 chrome law (UI_SPEC §3.10 Amendment 5): A5.1 flat chrome inside the pane, A5.2's four composition clauses, A5.4's "danger never colour alone".
"Hits must read" (the S2.6 feel rulings): panels 2–3 are the hit/contact reads; the UI-animation house rule (Tween, never per-frame) keeps the marker legal.
Tick cross-refs: panel 1 rows = S19 T7 (P8) + T-feel-5's breach read adjacency · panel 2 = T-feel-4's neighbour (the muzzle row) untouched · panel 3 = S22 A2's ram cue/spark.
Reversal of this whole composition: the panels fall back to today's silent behaviours (no feed push, marker only on the marked target, ram with no spark/cue).
